verdict.statement: Across 16 distinct US frames, the classifier's pervious share differs from NLCD by 6.7 pp on average (bias 3.1 pp) and its impervious share by 8.9 pp (bias -5.4 pp). 3 of 16 classified scores fall inside the reference score interval.

classification/C2-repeat-stability.title: Classifier stability on an identical frame

verdict.statement: The same frame received 15 distinct compositions in 24 classifications. Water ranged 0–45 pp and the score 16.7–35.2. Run-to-run variation is of the same order as the ±5 pp sensitivity default, and larger for water.
24 of 61 stored scores disagree with the current scorer by up to 15 points; 9 would change band. Stored scores cannot be trusted as current model output.

hydrology/H1-cross-model-consistency.title: Do the bulk budget and the routing engine agree on the same inputs?

verdict.statement: The two water models disagree on identical inputs: routed retention differs from bulk retention by up to 24.8 pp of frame rainfall, and the routed engine credits the same drawn intervention with 0.79–0.87× the bulk model's avoided runoff.

hydrology/H2-curve-number-benchmark.title: Fixed coefficients against the NRCS curve-number method

verdict.statement: The fixed coefficients leave the curve-number envelope for vegetation (40% of depths), soil (60% of depths), buildings (100% of depths), pavement (40% of depths). The linear model cannot reproduce the reference's depth dependence: it over-predicts pervious runoff in small storms and cannot show pervious surfaces saturating in large ones.

routing/R1-synthetic-terrains.title: D8 routing on terrains with known answers

verdict.statement: D8 failed 3 of 7 analytic cases: isolated-peak, flat, slope-with-pit. It conserves water in every case, but water that reaches a flat or a pit stops there instead of ponding and moving on.

routing/R2-resolution-sensitivity.title: Does routing change with grid resolution?

verdict.statement: Median rank correlation of flow concentration between low and high resolution is 0.46; median top-10% hotspot overlap is 0.19. At high resolution a median 81% of water ends in interior pits rather than leaving the extent.

routing/R3-dem-source-sensitivity.title: Does routing change with the elevation source?

verdict.statement: Across 48 areas, only a median 36% of cells keep the same D8 direction when the elevation source changes, although elevations differ by a median RMSE of 1.982 m. Flow concentration ranks correlate at median ρ 0.135.

routing/R4-311-association-development.title: Development: routed accumulation and reported street flooding

verdict.statement: Across 173 deduplicated street-flooding reports in 82 of 208 areas, routed accumulation AUC is 0.553 [0.496, 0.617] versus 0.642 [0.58, 0.699] for simple low elevation (difference -0.089 [-0.163, -0.002]). Routed accumulation does not locate reports better than the baseline.
